Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: Yes, we have a documented decommission flow for Dedicated tenants; I attached a current data map and our erase runbook so you can see the steps. High-level: 

1) Submit a region-affinity-revocation request (we use the HubSpot ticket linked below).
2) We schedule a planned maintenance window to quiesce writes and take a final snapshot.
3) Snapshot eviction + sanitization: we run our snapshot-sanitizer job (evict -> overwrite zero-bytes -> tombstone) and remove replication links.
4) Backup retention trimming: any longer-term backups are marked for expedited purge and removed according to the cust-deletion policy you select (standard 30d, expedited 0–72h for Dedicated).
5) Audit exports: we provide a deletion log + checksums and a signed attestation.

Please see the attached: atlas_data_map_v2.pdf and erase_runbook_v1.md. Can you confirm AtlasPay needs the expedited purge option and whether you require the attestation on company letterhead (we can route via DocuSign)?

Links: HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.com/deal/123456
Runbook (redacted): https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/region-decom-runbook

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want a walkthrough.

— Priya

On Wed, Jun 12, 2024 at 11:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: Yes, we have a documented decommission flow for Dedicated tenants; I attached a current data map and our erase runbook so you can see the steps.

Couple implementation notes from infra so expectations are precise: 

- Final snapshot: we take a point-in-time snapshot and keep it only long enough to validate that the eviction and sanitize jobs completed successfully (typically 6–24 hours unless expedited purge requested).
- Snapshot sanitization: our sanitizer runs block-level zeroing of freed blocks and rewrites metadata to prevent lazy recovery; we then tombstone the snapshot record. This is followed by an immediate scrub pass to verify zeroing.
- Replicated copies: for cross-region replicas we first sever replication; dependent volumes are flagged for asynchronous deletion. Remote replica queues can take up to an additional 12–48 hours to drain depending on queue backlog.
- Backups: logical backups stored off-cluster (long-term) require an explicit expedited purge command from the customer to override standard retention. For Dedicated tenants we can coordinate an expedited purge that attempts to remove logical backups within 72 hours; we commit to giving a purge completion ETA and evidence.
- Evidence package: deletion audit (JSON logs), snapshot checksums pre/post-sanitize, and a sanitized-snapshot manifest. We can also provide a signed attestation PDF.

Operational caveat: For customers with on-prem integration hooks (SFTP egress, external object stores) we only control copies inside Redwood infrastructure; you'll need to confirm any external buckets are removed on AtlasPay's side.

Tl;dr: We can do expedited purge and provide attestation; timeline depends on (a) replication backlog and (b) whether AtlasPay asks for forced removal of logical backups.

— Karthik (Infra)

Thanks — a few legal/compliance asks so we can finalize the attestation: 

1) Acceptance criteria: define the specific evidence fields AtlasPay needs in the attestation (e.g., tenant id, snapshot id, deletion timestamps, operator ID).
2) Audit bundle: can we include an export of the audit trail as a signed JSON with a Redwood hash (SHA256) so AtlasPay can independently verify immutability?
3) SLA on attestation delivery: we usually commit to 5 business days after the deletion run completes; is that acceptable to AtlasPay?

Priya — if AtlasPay wants the attestation on company letterhead or with additional identification (for regulatory audits), we will route through sales-legal and put it on DocuSign. Also flagging that for expedited purges we will require a one-time form signed by AtlasPay acknowledging the possible impact on recovery windows.
